recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It is a narrow source correction in the authoritative current Binary narrative and preserves later Binary REST behavior clarifications.
issue_request: FHIR-17026 was a Published/Persuasive STU3 technical correction for FHIR-core Binary. It requested changing "slightly differently to all other resources on the RESTful API" to "slightly differently from all other resources when using the RESTful API", explaining that standard US English uses "differently from" and that "on the RESTful API" was awkward.
initial_application: The issue was initially applied in git-svn revision 14344 as commit 550ec164799f51e7635fe735066c5e108c539e65, which changed "differently to" to "differently from" in source/binary/binary-notes.xml but left "on the RESTful API" in place. Later the same day, revision 14354 (commit 4c0d34042c3e8742eda89fdb336da09c622aa009 for FHIR-13507 and FHIR-16886) restructured the Binary REST section and preserved that remaining wording.
additional_context: Binary is an active current-build resource in source/fhir.ini, including active resource, normative-package, first-normative-version, compartment-code, and standards-status entries. The same-day FHIR-13507 and FHIR-16886 Binary REST clarifications explain the paragraph rewrite but do not reverse FHIR-17026's editorial decision. Zulip and Confluence searches found no FHIR-17026-specific community record or conflicting work-group discussion; one 2016 Zulip thread quoted the pre-fix Binary wording as part of Binary retrieval behavior discussion.
reconciliation: Changed source/binary/binary-notes.xml so the introductory Binary REST sentence now reads "Binary resources behave slightly differently from all other resources when using the RESTful API:". This completes the remaining accepted wording correction without changing the surrounding conformance guidance.
source_changes: source/binary/binary-notes.xml: changed the Binary REST introduction from "from all other resources on the RESTful API" to "from all other resources when using the RESTful API".
